personality_one_liner: A deceptive, ultra-premium cinematic lock screen concealing a powerful command center for theatrical performances.

spacing.rule: Generous spacing for tap targets (essential for performers relying on muscle memory). Maintain strict alignment for the passcode grid.

do's: Use frosted glass on the Performer Setup screen headers and Peek view data table rows.
Apply glass effects strictly for performer-facing elevated surfaces.
dont's: NEVER use glassmorphism on the Spectator Lock Screen; it must remain completely flat, dark, and raw to sell the OS illusion.
Avoid heavy blur on small text layers.

screens.name: Spectator Lock Screen (Performance Mode)
screens.purpose: A deceptive, completely unbranded OS-style passcode screen that spectators interact with in dim lighting.

states.loading: Dark screen, no visible spinners (kills the illusion).
states.empty: Default state showing empty passcode indicator circles.
states.error: Uses a subtle left-right shake animation on the indicator dots.

screens.layout: Flex column architecture. Top flex: 1 for the prompt text and dynamic passcode indicator dots (empty circles that fill upon entry). Middle flex: 2 for the 3x4 numeric keypad. Use large circular hit areas. Bottom area holds 'Emergency' and 'Cancel'/'Delete' text buttons. STRICT MONOCHROME NO BRAND COLORS.

screens.name: Simulated Unlocked Screen
screens.purpose: The fake 'home' state that appears upon successful entry, giving the performer time to access the hidden peek.

states.empty: Shows an abstract dark cinematic background to simulate a clean home screen.

screens.layout: Full-bleed background image with a vertical gradient scrim overlay to maintain darkness. Entire screen wrapped in a Pressable with delayLongPress={2000} to trigger the hidden Peek view.

screens.name: Hidden Peek View
screens.purpose: A covert, highly glanceable summary table for the performer to instantly read the reconstructed values.
screens.layout: Dark utility layout. Oversized display typography at the top for the main reconstructed value. Below it, a clean glass-morphic list/table mapping original positions, mock dates, and source events. Designed for single-glance readability.

screens.name: Performer Setup Screen
screens.purpose: A premium command center where the performer configures trick modes, lengths, and offsets.
screens.layout: iOS Settings style but cinematic. surfaceSecondary grouped cards for segmented controls (Basic/Transform/Scramble/Hybrid), toggles for haptics/sounds, and input fields for offsets. KeyboardAvoidingView used to prevent overlay issues during offset entry.

unlocked_background.alt: A black and white abstract cinematic dark texture background

instructions_to_main_agent: CRITICAL: The Spectator Lock Screen must NOT use the brand color (Antique Gold). It must be strictly monochrome (surface and onSurface) to sell the illusion of a native OS lock screen.

Wire haptics directly to the keypad interaction. Every digit press must trigger a 'selection' haptic. A wrong passcode must trigger a 'notificationError' haptic alongside a Reanimated shake on the passcode dots.
For the Performer Setup screen, use iOS-style grouped lists but layered over the deep black/dark espresso backgrounds. Use brandPrimary for active toggle states.
Hide the Peek View via a strict 2-second long-press (delayLongPress={2000}) on the Simulated Unlocked screen.
Ensure large, forgiving tap targets (hitSlop) on the passcode keypad, as performers and spectators will use it by muscle memory or under pressure.
Use Geist font for all numeric readouts to ensure absolute precision, tabular alignment, and an OS-level aesthetic.
Do not include standard app navigation elements (headers, tab bars) on the Spectator Screen or Unlocked Screen. Maintain a completely immersive, edge-to-edge experience.
